9	## Chosen fix: Loop: auto-run full test suite after any turn with a successful edit; finish on green
10	
11	File: `mend/worker.py`
12	
13	In solve_task, after the per-block tool loop builds tool_results and before appending the user message, add an automatic verification step:
14	(1) Track `edited_this_turn = True` whenever an edit_file/write_file call in this turn succeeded, and `ran_full_suite_this_turn = True` whenever the model itself called run_tests with no pattern in this turn.
15	(2) If edited_this_turn and not ran_full_suite_this_turn, call `auto = run_tests_tool(work)`. This is the existing traced span, so it shows up in the trace. Append a text block to tool_results after all tool_result blocks: {"type": "text", "text": "Automatic full test run after your edit(s):\n" + auto}. If auto.startswith("PASSED"), set suite_passed = True.
16	(3) Keep the existing early exit: `if suite_passed and edited` returns with stop='suite_passed'.
17	(4) Update the edit_file and write_file tool descriptions in TOOLS to say: "After any turn containing a successful edit, the full test suite is run automatically and its result is returned to you; do not call run_tests yourself to verify. If the change needs several edits, make them all in this same turn so the automatic run sees the complete fix."
18	Do not change MAX_TURNS or other tools.
19	
20	Why it is general: Every bug fix ends with an edit followed by a verification run. Folding that run into the edit turn saves one model turn on every task, along with its full-context LLM call. Telling the model that the suite runs after each edit turn also nudges it to batch multi-part edits into one turn, since a partial edit produces a visible failure. Nothing here depends on the library, a module or a particular bug, and it builds on the kept stop-on-green rule rather than repeating it.

92	def _safe_path(work: Path, rel: str) -> Path:
93	    """Resolve a tool-supplied path, refusing anything outside the sandbox copy."""

145	    return len(line) - len(line.lstrip())

148	def _edit_ignoring_whitespace(target: Path, path: str, text: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
149	    """Fallback when `old` has no exact match: match line by line ignoring surrounding whitespace,
150	    re-indent `new` to fit, or explain precisely how `old` differs from the file."""
151	    old_lines = old.rstrip("\n").split("\n")
152	    file_lines = text.split("\n")
153	    stripped = [line.strip() for line in file_lines]
154	    want = [line.strip() for line in old_lines]
155	    n = len(old_lines)
156	    hits = [i for i in range(len(file_lines) - n + 1) if stripped[i : i + n] == want]
157	    if len(hits) > 1:
158	        starts = ", ".join(str(i + 1) for i in hits)
159	        raise ValueError(f"`old` matches (ignoring whitespace) at lines {starts}; include more surrounding context")
160	    first = next((k for k, w in enumerate(want) if w), None)
161	    if not hits:
162	        match = difflib.get_close_matches(want[first], stripped, n=1, cutoff=0) if first is not None else []
163	        if not match:
164	            raise ValueError("`old` not found in file; re-read the exact lines and copy them verbatim")
165	        line_no = stripped.index(match[0])
166	        actual, mine = file_lines[line_no], old_lines[first]
167	        raise ValueError(
168	            f"`old` not found. Closest line in the file is line {line_no + 1}: {actual!r} "
169	            f"(leading spaces: {_indent(actual)}); your first line was {mine!r} (leading spaces: {_indent(mine)}). "
170	            "Copy the text exactly as shown."
171	        )
172	    i = hits[0]
173	    delta = 0 if first is None else _indent(file_lines[i + first]) - _indent(old_lines[first])
174	    new_lines = new.rstrip("\n").split("\n") if new.rstrip("\n") else []
175	    if delta > 0:
176	        new_lines = [" " * delta + line if line.strip() else line for line in new_lines]
177	    elif delta < 0:
178	        new_lines = [line[min(-delta, len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))) :] for line in new_lines]
179	    file_lines[i : i + n] = new_lines
180	    target.write_text("\n".join(file_lines), encoding="utf-8")
181	    return (
182	        f"edited {path}: replaced {n} line(s) with {len(new_lines)} line(s) (note: your `old` had different "
183	        f"indentation than the file; matched ignoring whitespace and re-indented `new` by {delta:+d} spaces)"

205	def solve_task(task_id: str, report: str, work: Path) -> dict:
206	    """Run the agent loop on one task. Returns turns, tokens, stop reason and the trace id."""
207	    result = {"task_id": task_id, "trace_id": current_trace_id(), "turns": 0,

209	    files = list_files(work)

213	    while result["turns"] < MAX_TURNS:

215	        extra = {} if MODEL.startswith("claude-haiku-4-5") else {"output_config": {"effort": "medium"}}  # Haiku 4.5 rejects effort
216	        response = client().messages.create(

218	        )
219	        result["input_tokens"] += response.usage.input_tokens
220	        result["output_tokens"] += response.usage.output_tokens
221	        result["stop"] = response.stop_reason
222	        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})
223	        if response.stop_reason != "tool_use":
224	            result["summary"] = next((b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text"), "")
225	            return result
226	        tool_results = []
227	        suite_passed = False
228	        for block in response.content:
229	            if block.type != "tool_use":

232	                content, is_error = HANDLERS[block.name](work, **block.input), False
233	            except Exception as exc:  # report tool failures back to the model, don't crash the run
234	                content, is_error = f"Error: {exc}", True
235	            if not is_error and block.name in ("edit_file", "write_file"):
236	                edited = True
237	            if block.name == "run_tests" and not block.input.get("pattern") and content.startswith("PASSED"):

240	        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": tool_results})
241	        if suite_passed and edited:  # full suite green after an edit: done, skip the verify/summary turn

243	            text = "".join(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text")

254	    result["passed"], _ = run_tests(work)

content.text:
I made the 'Chosen fix' in `mend/worker.py` and changed no other file. As you asked, I didn't run anything, so it hasn't been tested.

- **Two new flags in `solve_task`:** each turn now tracks `edited_this_turn` (a successful `edit_file`/`write_file` call) and `ran_full_suite_this_turn` (the model called `run_tests` with no pattern).
- **Automatic test run:** if the model edited a file but didn't run the full suite itself that turn, the loop calls `run_tests_tool(work)`. Its result goes into `tool_results` as a text block after the tool results, starting "Automatic full test run after your edit(s):". If that result starts with `PASSED`, `suite_passed` is set.
- **Early exit:** the existing `suite_passed and edited` exit is unchanged, so a passing run still stops with `suite_passed`.
- **Tool descriptions:** `edit_file` and `write_file` now end with the sentence from the diagnosis. I put it in one shared `_AUTO_TEST_NOTE` constant so it's written only once.

`MAX_TURNS` and the other tools are unchanged.
